fullPassage: People have a need to maintain an image of self-integrity. In an early demonstration of this, Steele (1975) threatened women's self-images by telling them that, as members of their community, it was common knowledge that they either were cooperative with community projects, uncooperative with community projects, or not concerned about driving safely. A fourth, control group received no information relevant to their self-images. Two days later, a fellow researcher called each woman, asking her to list every food item in her kitchen to help a food cooperative. Women who had been told they were uncooperative people or careless drivers two days earlier helped the researcher almost twice as much as women in the other groups. Steele explains this effect in terms of the women's motive to restore their self-concepts as cooperative people.
